items.title: MACC proposes six governance reforms to strengthen cooking oil subsidy scheme
items.summary: The recommendations were presented by MACC's Governance Investigation Division following a review of the scheme implemented under the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry. Division director Datuk Mohd Zaki Hassan said the review focused on policy and quota management, licensing and permits, supply and distribution, sales and subsidy claims, monitoring and enforcement, as well as the effectiveness of the eCOSS system. He said the commission also proposed upgrading eCOSS into a comprehensive end-to-end subsidy management system covering quota applications, supply, distribution, sales records, credit notes, subsidy claims, payments, inspections and enforcement to ensure all subsidy transactions are digitally verified and processed through a secure and integrated platform.

items.title: High bills, cheap panels drive a Philippine solar surge
items.summary: EDWIN Salas watched as the first of 20 solar panels was installed on the roof of his home, joining a Philippine solar energy boom sent into overdrive by the Middle East war. "For years, rooftop solar was often framed as an environmental choice... today, it's a practical response to financial pressure," Brenda Valerio, country director for non-profit New Energy Nexus, told AFP. The Philippines this year became China's number two buyer of solar panels, according to a report from global energy think tank Ember.

items.title: Man suffers burns in fire that damaged five RAKR houses in Seberang Jerteh
items.summary: Jertih Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) Chief Mustafa Ismail said his team received an emergency call at 10.28am and arrived at the location at 11.44am, before successfully controlling the fire about 30 minutes later. “The fire involved five permanent residential houses, with one house completely destroyed and another almost completely destroyed, while the other three suffered damages ranging between 5 and 50 per cent,” he said. “A total of 14 firefighters and personnel along with two fire engines from the Jertih and Besut fire stations were involved in the firefighting operation, which utilised water from a nearby fire hydrant.

items.title: Rakuten values United Asiapac at 50 sen ahead of ACE debut
items.summary: The firm's valuation is based on a 15-time price-earnings multiple applied to United Asiapac's forecast earnings per share for the financial year ending 2027. Rakuten Trade vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the valuation is based on a 15 times price-earnings ratio applied to United Asiapac's financial year 2027 (FY27) forecast earnings per share. He said United Asiapac is licenced by both Petronas and Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros), allowing the company to undertake projects across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.

items.title: Kelington unit to build US$29.3mil air separation unit plant in India
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kelington Group Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary Ace Gases Technologies Pte Ltd will construct a 300 tonnes per day merchant air separation unit (ASU) plant worth US$29.3 million (RM120 million) in Maharashtra, India. The integrated engineering solutions provider said an ASU plant is an industrial facility that separates atmospheric air into its primary component gases, such as nitrogen, oxygen, and argon. "The ASU plant will be developed as a standalone merchant plant on a site spanning approximately 20,000 square metres, enabling Kelington to serve a broad base of industrial gas customers across Maharashtra and neighbouring markets.

items.title: Indonesia's Q2 2026 GDP growth accelerates to 5.29pct
items.summary: From the production side, he said manufacturing remained the largest source of growth, contributing 0.90 percentage points after expanding 4.52 per cent y-o-y and accounting for 18.50 per cent of GDP. "On the expenditure side, household consumption was the largest contributor to economic growth, growing 5.06 per cent y-o-y, contributing 2.67 percentage points to growth, and accounting for 53.32 per cent of GDP," he said. M Edy said gross fixed capital formation contributed 2.06 percentage points to economic growth, while government consumption contributed 1.07 percentage points, whereas net exports subtracted 0.78 percentage points.

items.title: Viral e-rider dispute at BPoint not on MBJB land, says city council
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The Johor Baru City Council (MBJB) has clarified that a viral altercation involving an e-rider selling packet drinks at BPoint occurred on privately-owned property. In a statement, MBJB said checks found that the location shown in the video, including the parking area where the incident occurred, was privately owned and not administered or managed by the council. MBJB said it issues business licences to traders operating at BPoint, with all licences registered under Malaysian citizens.

items.title: Fahmi: PKR congress to assess party performance in Johor, Negeri Sembilan polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The upcoming PKR national congress is expected to look into the party’s performance in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections and also the federal government’s policies, said PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. “Delegates, especially from Johor and Negeri Sembilan, are expected to share their views and experiences to identify weaknesses and propose improvements for the party. He said that the congress is also likely to see proposals from delegates regarding improvements to government policies.

items.title: East Asian LNG prices edge higher on heat, geopolitical risk: Rystad Energy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The East Asian liquefied natural gas (LNG) price for October delivery edged up 0.4 per cent week-on-week to US$20.4 per million British thermal units (MMBtu) on Aug 3, as geopolitical risk and extreme heat continued to support spot demand, according to Rystad Energy. In its Gas and LNG Market Update report, Rystad Energy noted that buying interest has expanded even though prices remain close to the US$20 per MMBtu mark. Rystad Energy analyst for Gas and LNG Research, Antonia Syn, said gas markets are being pulled in two directions at the moment, balancing weather-driven demand against escalating geopolitical risks.

items.title: China complains to Japan over defence white paper
items.summary: BEIJING: China's foreign ministry on Wednesday said it had complained to Japan about Tokyo's newly released defence white paper, accusing it of playing up a Chinese threat and making "unwarranted comments" about Taiwan. The paper states that the "overall military balance between China and Taiwan is rapidly tilting in China's favour." In a response to Reuters regarding the white paper, China's foreign ministry said Tokyo has no right to comment on the Taiwan issue as it is purely China's internal affair.

items.title: [UPDATED] Tabung Haji-linked firm's ex-CFO questioned for second day by MACC
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission today continued recording the statement of the former chief financial officer of a government-linked company as part of its investigation into the alleged abuse of power involving the RM370 million acquisition of shares in two plantation companies. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the former CFO arrived at the commission's headquarters about 10.30am. Halim said the former CFO has been instructed to return to MACC headquarters at 10am tomorrow for the continuation of the statement recording.

items.title: PM directs Human Resources Ministry to expedite 15,000 foreign worker applications, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma) to immediately process the first 15,000 foreign worker applications to address labour shortages in key sectors and support Malaysia’s economic activities. Communications Minister and Madani Government spokesperson Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the move was aimed at meeting workforce demand across affected industries. Prior to this, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan announced that Kesuma had assumed full responsibility for managing the One-Stop Centre (OSC) for Foreign Worker Management with immediate effect, following a Cabinet decision on July 1.

items.title: World faces fresh food price surge, FAO warns
items.summary: FRANKFURT: The world is on the verge of another bout of food inflation as wars in Iran and Ukraine along with El Nino create a perfect storm of higher costs and lower crop yields, the chief economist of the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation said. Food prices were a key driver of the 2022 global inflation surge but have been relatively benign so far this year, even tempering in some places the surge caused by high energy costs. "I expect that commodity prices will start to increase more now ... and food prices will start increasing by the end of the year, and next year for sure they will increase more," Maximo Torero told Reuters in an interview.

items.title: A-G must explain Nicky Liow's DNAA, say NGOs
items.summary: They said Liow had faced 26 charges involving more than RM36 million under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001. The group said the issue was not the outcome of the case, but transparency, adding that the public was entitled to know why a RM36 million money-laundering prosecution was discontinued. The groups said the Liow case did not stand alone, claiming it reflected a pattern where serious corruption and money-laundering prosecutions were discontinued through DNNAs without public explanations.

items.title: SCIB bags Sabah school rebuilding job
items.summary: Belian Juta Sdn Bhd awarded the contract to SCIB's wholly-owned subsidiary SCIB Industrialised Building System Sdn Bhd (SIBS). The latest contract further strengthens SCIB's construction and EPCC project pipeline in Sabah, while reinforcing its track record in delivering public sector education infrastructure projects. Chairman Datuk Chong Loong Men said the contract reflects the continued confidence placed in SCIB's project execution capabilities within Sabah's public infrastructure sector.

items.title: Kedah family's disappearance may be linked to 'kutu' debts
items.summary: JITRA: Police have not ruled out "kutu" debts as a possible reason behind the disappearance of a family of three from Taman Desa Bayanmas in Bukit Kayu Hitam. Kubang Pasu police chief Superintendent Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said police had received a report against the wife from a person claiming to be a victim of the scheme. The matter came to light after the woman's 62-year-old father lodged a police report yesterday after failing to trace his daughter, son-in-law and grandchild.

items.title: Justice for Rocky: Animals lovers rally in front of Klang council office
items.summary: KLANG: Some 200 animal lovers and activists gathered outside the Klang Royal City Council (MBDK) demanding justice for Rocky, the dog which died during an enforcement operation in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah last week. The gathering came days after a video went viral showing Rocky's owner pleading with enforcement officers to release the dog. Rocky's death has ignited nationwide outrage over the treatment of stray animals and the standard operating procedures (SOP) employed by local authorities.

items.title: Russia steps up disinformation campaigns ahead of German elections, security sources say
items.summary: BERLIN: Russia is intensifying disinformation campaigns in Germany, German security sources told Reuters, ahead of state elections in which the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) appears set to make major gains. Germany is holding elections in Berlin, Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania next month. Moscow has consistently denied involvement in disinformation campaigns against the West.

items.title: Penang Second Bridge eastbound route to Batu Kawan closed Aug 8 night for Cultural Night Run
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 5 — The eastbound route on the Sultan Abdul Halim Mu’adzam Shah Bridge (JSAHMS), from Batu Maung to Batu Kawan, will be temporarily closed from 8pm on August 8 until 3am on August 9. However, the westbound route from Batu Kawan to Batu Maung will remain open, as will routes from Bandar Cassia and the Batu Kawan Industrial Park (BKIP) to the North-South Expressway (PLUS). JKSB advised motorists travelling from Penang island to the mainland during the closure to use the Penang Bridge.

items.title: Nanta: LPT2 concessionaire to review long-term safety measures after elephant collision
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The concessionaire of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2) has been instructed to immediately repair the damaged safety fence and review long-term measures to enhance safety following a collision involving a vehicle and a herd of elephants at Km274.6 northbound along the Cheneh-Chukai stretch last night. Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said an inspection at the site found that the existing safety fence had collapsed, believed to have been damaged after being struck by the herd of elephants passing through the area. As an initial preventive measure, he said the LPT2 concessionaire has also been instructed to increase the frequency of patrols, particularly at night, in high-risk areas to monitor wildlife movement and ensure the safety of highway users.

items.title: Works minister: LPT2 concessionaire to repair fence, review long‑term safety after elephant crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The concessionaire of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2) has been instructed to immediately repair the damaged safety fence and review long-term measures to enhance safety following a collision involving a vehicle and a herd of elephants at KM274.6 northbound along the Cheneh-Chukai stretch last night. Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said an inspection at the site found that the existing safety fence had collapsed, believed to have been damaged after being struck by the herd of elephants passing through the area. As an initial preventive measure, he said the LPT2 concessionaire has also been instructed to increase the frequency of patrols, particularly at night, in high-risk areas to monitor wildlife movement and ensure the safety of highway users.

items.title: Rocky's death sparks probe into dog-catching SOP
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: The owner of Rocky, a pet dog allegedly beaten to death during an attempt to catch stray dogs in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah, Port Klang, has called for a transparent investigation into the incident. S. Roghini Devi, 42, said she returned home on July 29 and found Rocky restrained with a snare around his neck. Roghini said she was awaiting the veterinary report from the Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) and a full police investigation.

items.title: Teacher found dead in school toilet in Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING: A 55-year-old teacher was found dead inside a toilet at SMK Bau along Jalan Sebuku in Bau this morning. Wong Lee Choo was found unconscious on the toilet floor and later pronounced dead. "Upon opening the toilet door, the victim was found lying unconscious," he said.

items.title: Police submit investigation paper on Rocky's death to DPP
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The investigation paper into the death of a dog, known as Rocky, during a stray dog-catching operation on July 29 has been submitted to the deputy public prosecutor's office. South Klang police chief Assistant Commissioner Lim Jit Huey confirmed the matter, saying the report was submitted yesterday. "The investigation paper on Rocky's case was referred to the deputy public prosecutor's office yesterday.

items.title: Anwar orders HR Ministry to fast-track first 15,000 foreign worker applications
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has instructed the Human Resources Ministry to immediately process 15,000 foreign worker applications to meet urgent manpower needs in key sectors. "The prime minister has asked the Human Resources Ministry to immediately process the first 15,000 foreign worker applications. On July 6, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan announced that the ministry had assumed full control over foreign worker quota management following a cabinet directive on July 1.

items.title: Perhilitan tracking elephant herd after LPT2 MPV collision
items.summary: CHUKAI: The Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) is tracking a herd of wild elephants that was hit by a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) at Km274.6 of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2), near the Cheneh Toll Plaza interchange, last night. State Perhilitan director Dennis Ten Choon Yung said the department is using drones to monitor the location and movements of the herd in the vicinity of the accident site. Dennis said six Perhilitan personnel were deployed to the accident site from 12.30am today to carry out monitoring and control operations, including in the surrounding Cheneh area.

items.title: Immigration busts passport forgery syndicate in KL raids, arrests three, seizes 119 forged passports
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The Malaysian Immigration Department (JIM) detained three Indonesian nationals, including a man suspected to be the mastermind of a passport forgery syndicate, during operations at two locations around here last night. Its director-general, Datuk Zakaria Shaaban, said that three individuals involved, namely two men and one woman aged between 30 and 50, were detained during operations at 11 pm in Taman Sri Kuching and Taman Bukit Cheras, here. He also suspected that the syndicate mastermind is believed to have committed an offence under Section 12(1)(f) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, while two other foreign nationals are believed to have committed offences under Section 6(1)© of the Immigration Act 1959/63.

items.title: Brazil police probe plot to carry out election attacks
items.summary: SAO PAULO: Brazilian security officials said Tuesday they were investigating eight suspects of plotting on Telegram to carry out attacks in the capital during October's elections, in which President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is seeking a fourth term. Intercepted communications showed the suspects, aged 19 to 31, were planning "severe acts of violence" against the presidential palace, parliament, Supreme Court and various ministries in Brasilia, said Victor Fernandes, digital rights secretary with the justice ministry. He told a press conference that the suspects were members of "two public groups on the Telegram platform that shared information regarding the planning of attacks in Brasilia" during the election period.

items.title: Passport-forging syndicate mastermind among three arrested in KL
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has arrested the alleged mastermind behind a passport-forging syndicate in Kuala Lumpur, said Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban. The Indonesian man, believed to be the mastermind, was arrested under Section 12(1)(f) of the Passports Act 1966 for unlawful possession, control or retention of travel documents. The department seized 119 passports believed to be forged — comprising 85 Indonesian passports, seven Bangladeshi passports, 22 Myanmar passports, two Vietnamese passports, one Nepalese passport and two Indian passports.

items.title: Social media platforms told to automate scam, gambling content takedowns
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Social media platforms must prepare their systems for automatic takedown of identified scam and online gambling content to comply with online safety regulations. MCMC has issued the CPC and RMC under the Online Safety Act. "These two codes will ensure platforms comply with online safety regulations, including those relating to scam and online gambling content," he said at the post-Cabinet meeting press conference here today.

items.title: RHB unveils Malaysia's first bank-owned unified payment gateway
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: RHB Bank Bhd has launched RHB Pay, which it describes as Malaysia's first bank-owned unified online payment gateway. It allows businesses to accept digital payments through a single platform and receive funds directly into their RHB accounts. RHB group managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Mohd Rashid Mohamad said businesses undergoing digital transformation are increasingly seeking payment solutions that offer not only convenience and efficiency, but also greater security, reliability and control over cash flows.

items.title: [UPDATED] Rocky's owner mulls legal action after probe outcome
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: The owner of Rocky, a dog at the centre of a recent controversy, is considering legal action pending the outcome of ongoing investigations, her legal team said today. Lawyer Choo Dee Wei, who is representing Rocky's owner S. Roghini Devi, 42, said consultations were under way but any formal legal steps would only be taken after investigators conclude their enquiries. On possible legal routes, Choo said the team would assess whether standard operating procedures (SOPs) had been followed.

items.title: Turkish court ordered block of Istanbul Mayor Imamoglu's candidacy account
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Social media platform X said on Tuesday it was complying with a Turkish court order to block access in the country to jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu's presidential candidacy office account, but was challenging the order in court. An Istanbul court ordered X to restrict access to Imamoglu's account, which has around 225,700 followers, to protect national security and public order, according to a copy of the order posted by X. X said Turkish law required it to implement the restriction, but that it disagreed with the order and had started legal proceedings. Imamoglu's main X account, which had nearly 10 million followers, was blocked in Turkiye in May 2025 under a similar order.

items.title: Defence minister on two‑day visit to Hanoi to strengthen Malaysia‑Vietnam defence ties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin began a two-day official visit to Vietnam today to strengthen defence cooperation between the two countries. He said the visit marks his first official trip to Vietnam since being appointed Defence Minister. “Malaysia and Vietnam have long enjoyed close defence ties.

items.title: House fire in Sungai Bakap leaves one injured
items.summary: SUNGAI BAKAP: A terrace house was 50 per cent destroyed in a fire at Lorong Bakap Permai 9 here today, with one victim reported in the incident. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said an emergency call was received at 2.46pm and a team from the Sungai Bakap station despatched to the scene. "The fire involved a single-storey terrace house measuring about 70ft by 20ft.

items.title: Malaysia to discuss refugee repatriation plan with Myanmar junta, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The Malaysian government will hold talks with the Myanmar junta over the proposed repatriation of 5,000 refugees to the country, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. He said the Myanmar junta must also ensure that the refugees would not face any danger before the repatriation process could begin. On July 29, it was reported that the Myanmar junta had agreed to receive 5,000 Myanmar refugees from Malaysia.

items.title: Witness claims beatings, electric shocks while under protection programme
items.summary: TAWAU: A plaintiff's witness in a RM190 million civil suit involving former senior officers and intelligence personnel of the Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCom) claimed she was beaten, subjected to electric shocks and forced to take pills. In response, the witness said: "I don't remember." The witness disagreed.

items.title: 'Like I died and came back': Malaysian footballer struck by lightning
items.summary: TUMPAT: A 22-year-old footballer who survived a lightning strike that killed one player and injured 11 others in Sungai Golok said he felt like he had "died and come back to life". Recalling the incident, Mohamad Alif Ezzahan Zulkifli said he was standing about 2 metres from the player who died when lightning struck . He said the bolt struck about 10 minutes into the second half of the Golok FA Cup semi-final match, which had kicked off at 4pm Thai time.

items.title: Fahmi: Up to 40 MPs ready to debate Tabung Haji RCI report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said up to 40 parliamentarians have expressed their willingness to debate the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the Tabung Haji (TH) board at the Dewan Rakyat special sitting next week. He said the Cabinet was also informed that Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul had agreed for the special sitting to be held continuously without a break. Fahmi, who is also the unity government spokesman, said the public could follow the Dewan Rakyat special sitting through live broadcasts on all official media channels.

items.title: Fahmi says tighter airport security measures being considered after pilot’s arrest over alleged drug trafficking
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The government is considering several security measures to be implemented at airports following the recent arrest of a Malaysian pilot in Indonesia over alleged drug trafficking, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said more stringent aviation security measures, in addition to tighter screening protocols, were among the measures being considered. “This would involve deploying regular police personnel together with Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad (MAHB) Aviation Security (AVSEC) auxiliary police unit.

items.title: Federal police open five investigation papers over alleged Tabung Haji commercial crimes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Police have opened five investigation papers after receiving nine reports from Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), its subsidiary and members of the public over alleged commercial crimes, including matters raised in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH. Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said investigators were recording statements from witnesses in Malaysia and abroad, while obtaining relevant documents to complete the investigations. “Police are committed to ensuring that every investigation is conducted independently, transparently, professionally and in accordance with the law.

items.title: Johor police bust drug syndicate using vape cartridges, seize RM10.68m worth of drugs
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 5 — Police have busted a drug trafficking syndicate that used vape cartridges to distribute drugs following the seizure of various types of drugs worth RM10.68 million in an operation across Johor on Aug 2. Johor deputy police chief DCP Hoo Chuan Huat said the operation, which began at 11 am, was carried out at five separate locations in Johor Bahru, Kulai and Muar, and led to the arrest of five local men, one foreign man and one foreign woman, aged between 36 and 46. Police also seized 47 plastic bottles containing vape liquid, a glass bottle containing 127.55 litres of methamphetamine liquid, two plastic packets believed to contain cocaine, one plastic packet containing ketamine, and a vape liquid filling machine.

items.title: MOH upgrading health facilities in Sabah, Sarawak interior based on local needs, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The Health Ministry (MOH) is adopting a tailored approach to upgrading health facilities in the interior of Sabah and Sarawak by taking into account the geographical challenges and specific needs of each area, said Deputy Health Minister Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib. Through the Borneo Health Tour, she said the ministry found that each health clinic visited had its own specific needs, whether in terms of additional equipment, more personnel, expanded space or relocation from less suitable sites. “Every health clinic I have visited faces different constraints.

items.title: Deputy minister: Security laws must protect safety without undermining human rights
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Efforts to strengthen national security must not come at the expense of human rights, Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department for Law and Institutional Reform M. Kulasegaran said. He said both priorities must advance together through an effective, balanced and forward-looking legal framework. “Legal reform had become increasingly important as technology, society and security threats continued to evolve.

items.title: MACC remands three more over alleged RM450,000 misuse of penalty payments
items.summary: Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah issued the remand order until Aug 9 against the three men, who are in their 50s, following an application by the MACC at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court today. According to a MACC source, the three were arrested at the commission’s headquarters at about 6 pm yesterday. Meanwhile, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests and said the case was being investigated under Section 17(a) of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: High Court acquits temple chairman over alleged trespass at Sri Maha Mariamman temple
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 5 — The High Court today acquitted a temple chairman who had been charged with trespassing at the Sri Maha Mariamman Temple on privately owned land last year, Sinar Harian reported. Lawyer Latheefa Koya, who represented M Paramaguru, 49, said Justice Hazlina Hussain quashed the charge after finding it was fatally defective. In a statement, Latheefa said the court ruled the charge failed to disclose the criminal intent required to constitute the offence of trespass.

items.title: Selangor AI White Paper to outline landscape, map benefits, challenges, value proposition, says MB
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 5 — The Selangor government’s artificial intelligence (AI) White Paper, which is currently being developed, will outline the overall landscape for the use of the technology, including its challenges, benefits and value proposition. “The AI White Paper will serve as a guideline for us, particularly in Selangor, on how we should approach, live with and interact with AI,” he said. Amirudin said the AI White Paper would be tabled at the State Legislative Assembly for debate at a later date.

items.title: Cops investigate housebreaking, robbery in Tanjung Bungah; CCTV shows lone suspect in five‑day crime spree
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 5 — Police have opened investigation papers into four crimes reported in Tanjung Bungah between July 28 and August 2, involving housebreaking, robbery, trespassing and theft. Northeast district police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said two of the four cases resulted in losses estimated at about RM17,000, while the other two caused no losses, refuting claims circulating on social media that five incidents had occurred in the area. He said police believed a man wearing a red shirt seen in CCTV footage could be linked to some of the incidents, although investigations were ongoing to establish the connection.

items.title: Selangor fine‑tunes new model for WiFi Smart Selangor reimplementation, says state exco
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 5 — The Selangor government, through Smartsel Sdn Bhd, is fine-tuning a new model for the reimplementation of the WiFi Smart Selangor (WSS) initiative, taking into account various factors, including changing user needs. State Islamic Affairs and Innovation Committee chairman Mohd Fahmi Ngah said the new free WiFi model would also take into consideration usage levels at each location, infrastructure capacity, as well as a more sustainable funding and operational mechanism. Mohd Fahmi said the new model was developed after the state government decided to adopt a more sustainable and resilient service delivery model.

items.title: GOF seizes RM9.39m worth of illegal e‑waste in Ipoh raids, 14 arrested
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 5 — The General Operations Force (GOF) Northern Brigade seized 120,220 kilogrammes of electronic waste (e-waste) worth about RM9.39 million, along with processing machinery, during raids on three premises around Ipoh on Aug 3. Its commander SAC Balveer Singh Mahindar Singh said the operation also led to the arrest of 14 individuals aged between 20 and 50, comprising two local men believed to be the premises managers and 12 Myanmar workers, including eight men and four women. He said intelligence gathered over a week found that the three premises were allegedly processing e-waste without approval from the Department of Environment (DOE), while operating under the guise of recycling factories.

items.title: Ops Sapu: 81 undocumented migrants held at Kedah construction site
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 5 — The Kedah Immigration Department arrested 81 undocumented migrants during Ops Sapu at a construction site in Kuala Kedah yesterday. The department said the operation, which began at 9.50am, was carried out following intelligence gathering and public tip-offs, and involved 19 officers from its Immigration Action Unit under the Enforcement Division. “A total of 81 undocumented migrants were arrested, comprising 73 men and eight women, namely 42 Bangladeshis, 26 Indonesians, 10 Myanmar nationals, one Pakistani and two Indians,” the department said in a statement.

items.title: PLUS opens tenders for next phase of Juru-Sungai Dua traffic dispersal project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — PLUS Malaysia Bhd (PLUS) has opened tenders for Packages 2 and 5 of the Juru-Sungai Dua Traffic Dispersal Project (PTJSD) as the project enters its next phase, with Package 1 recording an overall physical progress of 34.63 per cent as of July 31. In a statement today, PLUS said the tender process for Packages 2 and 5 was underway, marking another milestone in the implementation of the project. Under Package 1, utility relocation works have reached 75 per cent completion, while geotechnical works along Jalan Tun Hussein Onn, including the construction of a new bridge, have achieved 68 per cent completion.

items.title: SPM 2025 holders can now apply for Public Service Dept’s Dermasiswa B40 scholarships until Aug 16
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 5 — The Public Service Department (PSD) has opened applications for the 2026 Dermasiswa B40 (DB40) programme for 2025 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) holders from eligible B40 families to pursue diploma studies at institutions of higher learning in the country. PSD said applications for the programme are open from 2pm on August 3, 2026 (Monday), until 5pm on August 16, 2026 (Sunday), via the PSD Sponsorship Portal at https://penajaan.jpa.gov.my . “Through the programme, students have the opportunity to pursue diploma studies at selected public universities, polytechnics, MARA TVET institutions and Public Skills Training Institutes (ILKA) in strategic fields that support the country’s human capital development,” PSD said in a statement.

items.title: Teen’s remand extended over death of newborn found with stab wounds in Kluang
items.summary: KLUANG, Aug 5 — A 19-year-old college student’s remand has been extended by one day to assist investigations into the death of a newborn baby found with stab wounds in a house toilet here late last month. The remand extension order was issued by Magistrate Nurasidah A. Rahman at the Magistrate’s Court here today. Further investigations at the rented house where the female student lived in Taman Setia Mutiara led to the discovery of a deceased female baby in the toilet.

items.title: Driver and wife injured after MPV hits herd of wild elephants on LPT2 near Chukai
items.summary: CHUKAI, Aug 5 — A couple were injured after their multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) collided with a herd of wild elephants at Kilometre 274.6 of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2), after the Cheneh Toll Plaza, near here last night. Kemaman police chief Supt Mohd Razi Rosli said the 10.20pm incident left Abdul Wahid Ismail, 55, with minor injuries to his left hand, while his wife, Fauziah Muda, 52, injured her right hand. “Initial investigations found that Abdul Wahid was driving a Toyota Estima MPV in the left lane when he came upon a herd of wild elephants on the road.

items.title: Car crashes into Klang pastry shop after driver selects wrong gear, injuring assistant
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 5 — A shop assistant was injured after a car crashed into a pastry shop in Taman Berkeley, Klang, at about 3.30pm yesterday. North Klang District Police chief ACP Ramsay Embol said the crash was believed to have occurred when a woman in her early 50s selected the wrong gear and accidentally pressed the accelerator while leaving a parking space outside the shop after making a purchase. “The shop assistant, a woman in her early 30s, was rushed to KPJ Klang Hospital for treatment, while the car driver, who was also injured, was taken to Sunway Medical Centre,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Rosmah seeks stay on RM67.4m ruling, cites RM100,000 bank balance and concerns over jeweller’s finances
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Counsel for Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor today sought a stay of execution on a court order requiring her to pay RM67.4 million to Lebanese jeweller Global Royalty Trading SAL, saying she has only about RM100,000 in her bank account and there is “simply no mechanism” to verify the Beirut-based firm’s financial standing. Rosmah’s lawyer Reza Rahim said the plaintiff’s affidavit failed to provide any details of its bank accounts, available funds or other assets, leaving no evidence that it could guarantee repayment of the RM67.4 million if Rosmah succeeded on appeal. Today was the High Court’s hearing of Rosmah’s application to stay the High Court’s decision from June 10 this year.

items.title: Man found dead at Tanjung Rambutan care facility, police launch murder probe
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 5 — Police have launched an investigation into the death of a 54-year-old local man at a nursing home in Tanjung Rambutan yesterday. In a statement today, Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said Tanjung Rambutan Police Station was informed by the Tanjung Rambutan Health Clinic about the death of a resident at the care facility at 2pm. He said initial police checks at the scene revealed several injuries on the victim’s body.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh announces nine more KL open spaces gazetted to protect green areas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The government is stepping up efforts to safeguard Kuala Lumpur’s green spaces with the gazettement of nine additional open areas, aimed at ensuring city development remains balanced while preserving public recreational areas. The nine newly gazetted open spaces include Lot 82448 in the Batu sub-district, near Desa ParkCity Lake (6,607 square metres or 1.632 acres); Lot 82443 in the Batu sub-district, also near Desa ParkCity Lake (22,000 square metres or 5.436 acres); Lot 202030 in the Setapak sub-district, near Bayu Sentul Condominium (13,882 square metres or 3.430 acres); and Lot 38500 in the Petaling sub-district, near Residensi Jalil Mas (529 square metres or 0.130 acres). Other newly gazetted open spaces include Lot 25119 in the Setapak sub-district, near Masjid Salahuddin Al-Ayubbi in Taman Melati (1,456 square metres or 0.359 acres); Lot 39399 in the Petaling sub-district, near East Bukit Jalil Condominium (1,658 square metres or 0.409 acres); Lot 39397 in the Petaling sub-district, also near East Bukit Jalil Condominium (185 square metres or 0.045 acres); Lot 56219 in the Batu sub-district, near United Point Mall (3,679 square metres); and Lot 482950 in the Kuala Lumpur suib-district, near Padang TURF Tasik Permaisuri (1,505 square metres or 0.371 acres).

items.title: Sanusi issues LODs to Nga Kor Ming, two others over alleged distortion of remarks
items.summary: ALOR STAR, Aug 5 — Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor has issued letters of demand (LOD) to DAP deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming and two others accused of distorting his remarks at a recent ceramah in Negri Sembilan, the New Straits Times reported. The report said Sanusi had also issued an LOD to Salim Abd Rahman, while former Skudai assemblyman Marina Ibrahim was scheduled to receive hers. Sanusi said those who distorted facts, embellished or twisted his statements would also receive LODs.
